openings.claim: Clamp closure may disturb an initially correct seat; continuous hand seating during closure could improve return without requiring tighter fit.
openings.delta: Keep the incumbent two stop-and-corner-datum pockets, movable clamps, threaded bolts and cord retention. Change the closing action: maintain hand pressure toward the insertion stop and both datum faces throughout tightening. Compare with seating, releasing that pressure, then tightening. The changed dependency is preservation of contact during closure, carried by the operator rather than surrounding fit.
openings.prediction: The nearest rival is inconsistent initial insertion seating. Closure disturbance predicts similar initial positions but larger before-to-after closure movement when seating pressure is released; initial-seating error predicts offsets already present before closure. Smaller final errors with maintained pressure support the intervention. No improvement, displacement preceding closure, or equal movement under both procedures defeats its proposed advantage. Neither pattern proves the cause; hand-force variation remains a confound.
openings.probe: Fabricate the incumbent within 100 minutes using only supplied materials. First verify the 90 mm envelope, hand exchange and captive components; unresolved geometry or inadequate stiffness prevents this probe. Use one joint with two closing procedures, alternating their order. Within twenty minutes, perform five exchanges per rod position under each procedure; substitute the 18 mm rod for the last two exchanges of the 19 mm position in each. Record pointer position after seating before closure, after closure, exchange duration, and four ten-second 10 N load trials per procedure. Never apply test load before clamping. Require every final return and loaded position inside the 2 mm circle, every exchange below forty seconds, and no freed component. If intermediate position cannot be observed without disturbing seating, the causal comparison is inconclusive.
assumptions: Shared fasteners, eight bolts, six plywood pieces and cord can make rigid captive pockets; this remains unverified.
One hand can maintain all datum contacts while the other tightens.
Measurement resolution and twenty-minute logging capacity may not distinguish closure movement.

assessment: A discriminating probe and possible assembly operation, not a deployment claim. No supplied observation establishes clamp-induced motion.

lineage.reason: Preserves the incumbent hardware concept while replacing its noncomparative performance probe with a closure-stage comparison.
